about: Lesson S19, LoRA and fine-tuning. Computed by tools/school/fill_lora.mjs from system/school/lora.mjs, lora-task.mjs and lora-measure.mjs and the attention lab's own model and trainer. Do not edit by hand. Losses are in nats (natural log). Every method starts from the same base weights and trains on the same task rows for the same steps.

recipe.lora: W_eff = W + (alpha / r) A B, A [inputs, r] uniform in +-1/sqrt(inputs), B [r, outputs] zero

task.about: The new task, "things keep their look": "the <thing> was <adjective> .", then 0 to 2 of the corpus's short guide sentences (tallow lit the lamp; rerun knocked twice; rerun knocked on a shell; pylon watched the dock; pylon stood on the dock), then the thing named again with the same adjective. The corpus's own distractor sentence draws a fresh adjective every time, so the base model has never seen a look kept. Every next word has exact odds by construction; floor is their loss on the task's own 256 held-out rows (6144 targets), idealAccuracy what the exact odds would score (a word with 10 equal choices counts a tenth). answer is the repeated adjective (certain once the thing is named again); repeatThing is the repeated thing. A first design with two things described and one asked about was dropped: no method, full fine-tuning included, learned to tell the two apart in 5,000 steps (all stalled at half right on the answer), so it could not compare methods.
task.exampleRow: the boat was bright . rerun knocked on a shell . the boat was bright . the boat was wet . rerun knocked on

base.about: The base model on the new task before any fine-tuning, and on the original 256 held-out rows of the corpus (origFloor is the corpus generator's own loss there). byRole splits the task score by word role.

methods.about: Every method fine-tunes a copy of the base on fresh task rows (data seed 300 + seed) for 1500 steps, batch 16, AdamW with the lab's warmup and clipping and no weight decay (decay would add a full-rank shrink to the change measured in rank). lr was picked per method from 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03 on seed 1 by the task loss on 256 separate validation rows (validLossByLr); seeds 2 and 3 then ran at that rate. lrAtGridEdge marks a pick at the smallest or largest rate tried, where a better rate may lie outside the grid. Seeds change the data stream and, for LoRA, the random A. trained counts the numbers each method changes (the base has 20864). lora.attn adapts the 4 attention projections, lora.all every dense matrix (attention, feed-forward, readout); both leave the embedding tables, biases and norms frozen. lastLayer trains layer 2's whole block, the final norm and the readout. Scored at the end on the task's held-out rows and the original held-out rows; mean, sd and range over 3 seeds.

forgetting.about: What fine-tuning on the new task alone cost on the original corpus: loss and look-back (copy) accuracy on the 256 original held-out rows, before (the base) and after each method, mean over 3 seeds. Training saw only task rows, so this is the worst case; mixing original rows into training was not tried.

rank.about: Hu et al.'s claim that the change a fine-tune makes has a low intrinsic rank, tested on the full fine-tune's change (fine-tuned minus base) of each dense matrix, 3 seeds. topK is the share of the change's squared size (sum of squared singular values) held by its top K directions; for90 is how many directions hold 90 percent. randomBaseline is the same for a matrix of independent random entries of that shape: the shares a change with no low-rank structure would show. truncated scores the full fine-tune with each dense matrix's change cut to its best rank-K version (other numbers kept), on the task. summary sets each LoRA rank's task loss beside it. This tests the claim for this model and this task only.

controls.about: Controls. stepZero: with B zero the adapted model's logits on all 256 task rows equal the base's bit for bit, for attention and every-matrix adapters at rank 1 and 8. gradCheck: central finite differences of the loss in every entry of all 18 adapter tensors (every dense matrix, rank 2, a small float64 model with large random weights and a nonzero B), worst tensor-level relative error; broken reads B with the wrong transpose in dA, which the check must catch. rank0: an adapter with rank 0 has no numbers to train; 50 steps leave the task loss where it was.

speed.about: Milliseconds per fine-tuning step in Node (V8), one process, nothing else running, 40 steps after 5 warm-up. Every method runs the model's full backward pass (the adapter gradient is read off the full weight gradient), so LoRA saves optimiser memory and trained numbers here, not step time. inPool is the mean per-step time inside the fill's runs (4 processes at once). A browser lab running 40 ms slices fits about 40 / ms steps per slice.

film.about: One matrix for the film: l1.wqkv (32 inputs by 96 outputs, stored row-major as [input][output]), the attention matrix whose change under full fine-tuning (seed 1) is largest by Frobenius norm (changeNorms lists all four). base is the pretrained matrix; fullChange is fine-tuned minus base; rank1 is the rank-1 adapter (lora.attn.r1, seed 1, lr 0.003) on that matrix: A has one number per input, B one per output, and its change is s times A B (s = alpha / r = 8). singular are all 32 singular values of fullChange, largest first.
